questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes how an **ogive** is constructed from a cumulative frequency table?

options.text: Points are plotted at the upper class boundary of each class with height equal to cumulative frequency, starting at height $0$ at the lower boundary of the first class.
Points are plotted at the class centres of each class with height equal to individual frequency.
options.why: Describes a frequency polygon rather than an ogive.

options.text: Points are plotted at the midpoints of cumulative frequency columns and anchored to the origin.
options.why: Ogives connect top-right corners (upper boundaries), not column midpoints.

options.text: Columns are drawn with gaps between them to represent cumulative running totals.
options.why: Histogram columns must touch with no gaps between continuous class intervals.

questions.solution_text:
An ogive connects the top-right corners (upper class boundaries) of cumulative columns, starting at (lower boundary, $0$).
Points are plotted at the upper class boundary of each class with height equal to cumulative frequency, starting at height $0$ at the lower boundary of the first class.
